content: Nevirapine is a medication used in combination with other HIV drugs to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, allowing the immune system to function more effectively. This helps lower the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves overall quality of life. However, it is important to note that nevirapine is not a cure for HIV. To reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to others, it is essential to continue taking all prescribed HIV medications as directed by your doctor. Additionally, use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity, and avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or bodily fluids. Before starting nevirapine, read the medication guide provided by your pharmacist and review it each time you get a refill. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablets. If you are taking nevirapine for the first time, you must begin with the immediate-release form for 14 days before transitioning to the extended-release form. If you have already taken the immediate-release form for more than 14 days, you can start the extended-release tablets immediately. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you stop taking this medication for more than seven days for reasons other than serious reactions (as described in the warning section), consult your doctor for instructions on restarting treatment. It is crucial to take this medication, along with other HIV medications, exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not skip doses, increase your dose, take it more frequently than prescribed, or stop taking it without your doctor’s approval. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Common side effects of nevirapine include tiredness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and, in rare cases, drowsiness. You may notice the empty extended-release tablet shell in your stool, which is normal. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune system may cause symptoms to develop. These reactions can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Nevirapine commonly causes a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish between a mild rash and a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. Although rare, a very serious allergic reaction to this drug may occur. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms of a severe allergic reaction. Nevirapine has been associated with rare but severe, and sometimes fatal, liver problems and skin/allergic reactions. Women are at a higher risk of developing these severe reactions. To reduce the risk of skin/allergic reactions, nevirapine is started at a lower dose for the first 14 days. Individuals with higher T-cell counts at the start of treatment are at greater risk for liver problems. The risk of these serious side effects is highest during the first 18 weeks of treatment, particularly in the first six weeks. If you have stopped taking nevirapine due to liver problems or skin/allergic reactions, you must never take any form of nevirapine again. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments so your doctor can monitor your response to the medication. Before taking nevirapine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Nevirapine may rarely cause drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can increase drowsiness. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing activities that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and nevirapine may be part of that treatment. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some medications can affect the removal of nevirapine from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include rifamycins (such as rifampin). Nevirapine can also speed up the removal of many other medications from your body, which may affect how they work. Do not use prednisone to prevent a rash, as it can increase the risk of a rash during the first six weeks of nevirapine treatment. This medication may decrease the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function, viral load, and T-cell counts, should be performed while taking this medication. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
